subject: Proposal: Platform lead consolidation and matrix reporting pilot
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-03 09:14 -07:00
Subject: Proposal: Platform lead consolidation and matrix reporting pilot

Team —

I wanted to surface a concrete proposal for how we handle the next phase of platform ownership: consolidate the four current functional platform leads into a smaller centralized "Platform Leadership Pool" and move to a matrix reporting model for day-to-day delivery. High level:

- What: Move from N functional leads (embedded per product area) to 2 central platform leads + 2 senior ICs with dotted-line relationships into product squads.
- Why: Reduce context switches, standardize runtime priorities (latency/cost), and give a single escalation path for infra incidents.
- Scope: Applies to Platform Compute, Serving Runtime, Observability, and Deploy Tooling teams.
- Timeline: pilot over 8 weeks, voluntary transfers + manager-led consultations, full decision after review.

Key asks:
1) HR & legal review of transfer mechanics and international constraints (Mina)
2) Engineering readiness/ownership gaps and pilot squad selection (Karthik + Grace)
3) Manager comms / performance-review alignment (Lauren)

I've attached org_chart_proposal_v2.pdf and impact_matrix.xlsx that map rough role moves and who is likely impacted in the short term. This is intentionally conservative and designed to preserve individual career paths while consolidating leadership.

Sensitive points I want us to coordinate tightly on:
- How this intersects with the upcoming performance review cycle (calibration, role changes during mid-cycle). We must avoid surprises to ICs.
- Any changes that look like demotions or removal of manager headcount — we need a clear career-preserving option (lateral moves, individual contributor tracks, or HR-mediated transition).
- EU/UK labor notice windows and local works council consultation if needed.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Mina: review policy and draft standard transfer language + suggested timeline by EOD Fri (4/9)
- Karthik & Grace: propose two pilot squads (one infra-heavy, one cross-product) by Tue (4/6)
- Lauren: draft manager talking points and a private manager-only Q&A doc by Wed (4/7)

I want to keep this tight and manager-first: no all-hands or broad comms until we have HR signoff. Thoughts?

— Logan
Logan Wright
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachments: org_chart_proposal_v2.pdf (pdf), impact_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03 11:02 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Platform lead consolidation and matrix reporting pilot

Thanks for the outline, Logan. High-level OK but several legal/comp implications we need to close before any manager-level 1:1s. Quick notes: 

- Transfers vs. role changes: For most US employees we can do a lateral reassign, but EU staff likely need consultation and potentially a works-council notification. If we have any German/Netherlands staff in impacted roles, expect a 4-week minimum consultation window.
- Compensation title parity: If a manager becomes a dotted-line IC lead, we need to preserve compensation or document the pathway to a matching title to avoid pay-equity concerns. HR will not move people into a lower grade without explicit bilateral agreement.
- Performance review cycle: We should not change reporting for anyone currently under active PIP or near promotion calibration; those cases require separate handling.
- Severance/notice: If any role is eliminated, we need early involvement from Finance for budgeted severance — but your proposal minimizes eliminations, so that helps.

Action items I can own:
1) Draft standard transfer consent language + FAQ for impacted employees by 2027-04-09.
2) Provide a country-by-country constraint matrix (EU/UK/CA/US) by 2027-04-08.
3) Join the pilot selection sync and confirm manager checklists.

One ask for Karthik: please provide a prioritized list of people who will be asked to consider dotted-line moves (names/grades) so we can pre-check constraints.

On the external side, I've looped in Lisa Monroe (HR Ops consultant) who has done similar transitions with tech orgs and can help with localized templates.

— Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, People Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-04 09:28 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: Platform lead consolidation and matrix reporting pilot

Appreciate the clarity, Logan. I support centralizing some platform leadership but we must protect line-of-ownership for critical SLOs. Concerns and suggestions: 

1) On-call/operational ownership: If platform leads are centralized, we need explicit handoffs and a written RACI for runbook ownership (incident commander, pager escalation). Otherwise we increase resolution time.
2) Two-phase pilot: pick one infra-heavy squad (Serving Runtime) and one cross-product squad (Embeddings/Indexing) so we can validate both operational and cross-functional behavior.
3) Headcount equivalence: ensure the two central leads have clear capacity for the current manager responsibilities. If we centralize 4 leads into 2, we need to confirm their spans won't exceed 12 directs in steady-state.
4) Performance calibration: Do not move anyone mid-cycle who is under active review. For people eligible for promotion in this cycle, let promotions complete then apply matrix move.

Deliverables I will own: pilot squad names + rationale by 2027-04-06; a draft RACI for incident ownership by 2027-04-09.

Also flagging a technical risk: the Observability team is due a major rollout in late May — avoid moving their lead into a pilot until post-release. I'll highlight candidates who are safe to move.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Hi Mina/Logan —

Quick note from HR Ops side: we can provide localized consent templates and a works-council engagement playbook. A few considerations from prior engagements: 

- Keep manager conversations human-first: provide talking points that open with career upside and pathing, then provide the structural rationale.
- Offer time-bound opt-in windows for voluntary transfers (e.g., 10 business days) and a fallback of a 'no change' option for anyone who prefers to stay in current reporting for 6 months.
- Document performance-review neutrality: transfers should not reset mid-cycle calibration — list these cases explicitly in the FAQ.

I have a template for consent + FAQ I can share (redacted) and a sample email cadence for manager comms. If you want, I can join the manager sync on 4/7 to walk through the scripts.

— Lisa Monroe
Founder, HR Ops Consulting

Thanks all for the quick reads and practical notes. Summarizing decisions and owners based on thread: 

- HR (Mina): produce transfer consent language, country constraints, and FAQ by 2027-04-09. Owner: Mina.
- Eng (Karthik): select two pilot squads and produce RACI for incident ownership by 2027-04-06 (pilot squads) and 2027-04-09 (RACI). Owner: Karthik.
- Manager comms (Lauren): draft manager-only talking points and a private Q&A doc for managers by 2027-04-07. Owner: Lauren.
- External support (Lisa): share consent template and join manager sync on 4/7. Owner: Lisa.

Immediate operational constraints we agreed on:
- No role/reporting changes for folks in active promotion or PIP windows.
- Observability lead excluded from pilot until after the May rollout.
- Any role-elimination conversation requires explicit Finance approval first.

Next meeting: manager-only sync scheduled 2027-04-07 10:00 -07:00 (30m). I will circulate the agenda and pared-down slide deck (consolidated org chart + impact matrix) and we will not communicate broadly before HR signoff.

I'll open a Confluence page for the thread and a JIRA (SUP-1234) to track individual cases. Please add names for pilot candidates into the spreadsheet I attached earlier.

— Logan
Logan Wright
VP, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
